n: ‘The LORD reigneth’ begins a group of ‘enthronement psalms’ (93, 95–99) celebrating God as King. He is dressed in majesty and strength like royal robes, and the world he founded stands firm.

f.g: Belted, as a warrior ties on his belt to prepare for action.

n: God’s throne is not new; it has existed from ancient times, because he himself is eternal.
The ‘floods’ — rivers and seas — roar and raise their waves. In ancient thought, raging waters symbolized chaos and forces opposing God.

f.g: The repetition imitates waves surging higher and higher.

n: However loud the waves, the Lord on high is mightier still. No chaos — in nature or in life — is beyond his control.

f.w: mightier than the noise of many waters

n: God’s ‘testimonies’ — his covenant laws — are completely reliable, and holiness is what suits his temple forever.

f.g: Holiness is fitting for your temple.
